headline: World Cup debutants Cape Verde hold Spain to 0-0 draw
summary: In a historic first-ever World Cup appearance, Cape Verde stunned the European champions and tournament favorites Spain in a goalless opening match of Group H.
details: Cape Verde achieved a historic result by securing a 0-0 draw against Spain in their opening game of Group H on Monday. The debutants managed to hold the European champions and one of the tournament's favorites to a stalemate.

Despite dominating possession, Spain struggled to break through. Their clearest chance came late in the first half when Ferran Torres hit the bar, and keeper Vozinha saved a header from Mikel Oyarzabal on the rebound.

Vozinha continued his impressive performance, denying both Torres and Aymeric Laporte to keep the game scoreless at the break. Even the introduction of Lamine Yamal failed to change the outcome for Spain.

The resilient Cape Verde side not only defended their goal but also created late chances of their own, threatening to cause an even bigger upset. This marks a famous point in their first-ever World Cup appearance.
The other two teams in Group H, Saudi Arabia and Uruguay, are scheduled to meet in Miami later on Monday.

headline_marked: UK to [[ban social media for under-16s]] to protect children
headline: UK to ban social media for under-16s to protect children
summary: Prime Minister Keir Starmer announces sweeping restrictions on platforms like TikTok and Instagram, aiming to "give kids their childhood back."
details: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer has announced a sweeping ban on social media sites for children under 16. The move targets platforms including TikTok, Snapchat, and Instagram, as well as restrictions on gaming and live-streaming sites.

Starmer stated that a full ban is the right choice to make children safer and happier, providing them more security and freedom to grow up. The ban could be in place by next spring, supported by new regulations due by the end of the year.

The restrictions will also include 'world-leading blocks' on livestreaming and preventing strangers from contacting children. Additionally, the government is considering overnight curfews and curbs on infinite scrolling for those under 18.

Messaging services like WhatsApp and Signal, as well as educational tools like YouTube Kids and Google Classroom, will not be affected by the ban. However, the ban will likely require expanded age checks for all users.
Tech giants like Meta, YouTube, and Snapchat have expressed concern, arguing that a blanket ban could push young people toward riskier, unregulated platforms that lack parental controls.

Some experts and psychologists doubt the effectiveness of the ban, citing Australia's experience where many young people remained online. Starmer acknowledged the difficulty of enforcement but believes it will change the long-term culture around social media.
